newsitem.title: NORWAY: Financial sector dominates Norway share market.
newsitem.headline: Financial sector dominates Norway share market.

text.p: The financial sector continued to dominate activity on the Oslo bourse on Friday as speculation over the Storebrand/Christiania Bank merger and other takeovers gathered pace.

Overall the market managed to hold in positive territory despite a retreat from the session's high following the release of U.S. data. The Total index closed 0.2 percent higher at 1,034.93 points in turnover of 1.64 billion crowns.
Insurer Storebrand, Fokus Bank, morgage lender BNbank and Christiania Bank accounted for 864 million crowns of the day's turnover.

A five million block of Storebrand preference stock moved early in the session and sources said state pension fund, Folketrygdfondet, was the likely buyer. Folketrygdfondet held 7.81 percent in Storebrand before the acquisition.
The preference shares closed 5.30 percent up at 14 crowns.
Market players speculated that Storebrand's major shareholders are either moving to block the fusion or are shuffling for position on the board of the new merged company.
Trade was a heavy 240 million crowns in Fokus Bank and dealers said a major Swedish player was expected to make a bid for Norway's fourth largest commercial bank.
